options.metric: Annual total number of motorist deaths recorded in NYC police-reported crashes; sum number_of_motorist_killed.
options.denominator: None; an annual count, not a rate.
options.reason: A direct annual death count is a defensible way to describe the recorded fatality burden without implying an exposure denominator the data does not contain.
options.answer: This file cannot establish per-mile motorist fatality risk because it has no miles-driven data; its annual death-count proxy is 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025, with 139 in 2020.
options.interpretation: Per-mile risk cannot be determined because the file contains no miles-driven exposure; the plotted substitute is the annual total of recorded motorist deaths, summing number_of_motorist_killed across every NYC police-reported crash dated in 2013-2025, with no denominator and grouped by calendar year. The count was 110 in 2013, reached 139 in 2020, and was 81 in 2025, making this a measure of recorded fatality burden rather than travel-adjusted risk. The check covers 2,132,218 crash rows; annual rows rose from 203,742 in 2013 to a peak of 231,564 in 2018 and then fell to 85,546 in 2025, so the raw counts come from substantially different numbers of reported crashes. No planned rows were dropped for missing crash dates or motorist-death values (0 of 2,132,218 death values missing); all years span observed January 1 through December 31 dates, so all rows within the date range were kept, while dates outside 2013-2025 are out of scope and full date spans do not prove complete crash capture.

options.metric: Annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed divided by the number of police-reported crash rows, multiplied by 1,000.
options.denominator: All NYC police-reported crash rows dated in the same calendar year; scaled per 1,000 crash rows.
options.reason: Normalizing deaths by reported crashes gives a crash-based comparison that accounts for changing numbers of recorded crash rows, while remaining explicit that it is not a per-mile rate.
options.answer: This file cannot establish per-mile risk; instead, recorded motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crash rows were 0.540 in 2013 and 0.947 in 2025, reaching 1.273 in 2023.
options.interpretation: Per-mile risk cannot be determined because miles driven is absent; this chart instead shows the annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed divided by all NYC police-reported crash rows dated in that year, multiplied by 1,000, grouped by crash year from 2013 through 2025. The value was 0.540 deaths per 1,000 reported crashes in 2013, peaked at 1.273 in 2023, and was 0.947 in 2025; this is a defensible deaths-per-reported-crash measure, not risk per mile or per journey. Annual denominator rows rose from 203,742 in 2013 to 231,564 in 2018, then generally contracted to 85,546 in 2025, including a sharp drop to 112,918 in 2020; because the number of reported crash rows per year changes substantially, this rate compares deaths per recorded crash rather than changes in travel exposure. The check found no missing crash dates or motorist-death values among 2,132,218 planned rows (0 of 2,132,218 death values missing) and observed January 1-December 31 spans in every year, so all dated rows were retained with no missing-value exclusions; records outside 2013-2025 are out of scope, and the date spans do not prove complete crash capture.
